products.section_lead: Start with a small shuttle, or help form a full commuter line when seat demand is real.

items.title: N30 Executive Shuttle
items.body: Eight seats. On-demand. Prove the water commute for leadership teams, hybrid pods, or a campus pilot — without waiting for a full line.

items.title: N45 Commuter Line
items.body: Twenty seats. Scheduled corridor service when a line has enough committed seats. Built for campus-scale commute benefits — not a one-off charter.

anchor.title: Option B — Anchor a line
anchor.body: Underwrite a vessel, brand the service, and help shape the service window for a full line.

copy.hero_headline: The Bay is the fastest lane your team isn't using.
copy.hero_sub: A connected commuter water network for Bay Area employers — electric hydrofoil vessels, terminal-to-terminal, faster than the bridge at rush hour.
copy.stripe_lesson: In 2024 we ran the first employer water commute on the Bay — daily service for Stripe employees, North Bay to Oyster Point. The ride delivered: smooth, quiet, four feet above the chop, a desk on the water. One structural lesson, stated plainly: we flew an eight-seat executive vessel on a mass-commute job. Commuter-line economics need our twenty-seat vessel, built for exactly this. The ride worked. The vessel class is what we fixed.
copy.loi_cta: We are sequencing the first commuter lines now. A letter of intent is non-binding — it costs nothing and commits nothing. It tells us which line to light up first and how many seats employers want on day one. Option A: reserve seats for your team on a line. Option B: anchor a line — underwrite the vessel, brand the service, shape the service window.
copy.price_anchor: roughly a parking space — often less

problem_chips.label: Water is about twice conventional ferry speed
Foiling above chop — smooth enough to work

copy.launch_trigger: A line launches when about 60–80 seats are committed — enough for a real commuter service, not a thousand-seat fantasy.
copy.problem_title: The bridge is the bottleneck. The Bay is the spare lane.
copy.problem_lead: Your people already live and work on water-adjacent campuses. Rush-hour road time is the tax. Water cuts that tax — quietly, on a service window you help form with seat interest.
copy.proof_lead: The Stripe pilot is public record. We keep the lesson as plain as the ride was smooth.
copy.proof_worked_body: Smooth, quiet, four feet above the chop — a real desk on the water for a daily employer commute.
copy.proof_fixed_body: Commuter service needs the twenty-seat vessel, not an eight-seat executive shuttle on a mass-commute job.
copy.proof_ask_body: Non-binding seat interest so we light the right line first — not a thousand-seat fantasy trigger.
copy.network_lead: Connected Bay Area stations — Marin, SF, East Bay, Peninsula, and South Bay — on real or planned ferry landings. Gold rings mark transfer hubs (Ferry Building, Mission Bay, Oyster Point, Oakland JLS). Marin ends at Ferry Building; Biotech meets Peninsula at Oyster Point. Use phase control for launch vs full build-out (Carquinez + deep South Bay).

copy.calc_lead_html: Planning defaults reproduce a worked example of $4,500/mo net incremental — about $75 per rider. Change the inputs; the math stays the same.
